    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2006.16925v3</id>
    <title>Ethical Analysis on the Application of Neurotechnology for Human Augmentation in Physicians and Surgeons</title>
    <updated>2024-09-18T23:37:41Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.16925v3" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2006.16925v3" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>With the shortage of physicians and surgeons and increase in demand worldwide due to situations such as the COVID-19 pandemic, there is a growing interest in finding solutions to help address the problem. A solution to this problem would be to use neurotechnology to provide them augmented cognition, senses and action for optimal diagnosis and treatment. Consequently, doing so can negatively impact them and others. We argue that applying neurotechnology for human enhancement in physicians and surgeons can cause injustices, and harm to them and patients. In this paper, we will first describe the augmentations and neurotechnologies that can be used to achieve the relevant augmentations for physicians and surgeons.
